chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say to me: 'Let poverty/neediness towards people and self-sufficiency from them gather in your heart, so that your neediness towards them is in the softness of your speech and the goodness of your countenance, and your self-sufficiency from them is in the purity of your honor and the preservation of your dignity.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, who said: 'Ali ibn Umar narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:'
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say, then mentioned something similar.

key_terms.الِاسْتِغْنَاءُ: Self-sufficiency or independence from others, fostering dignity
key_terms.الِافْتِقَارُ: Neediness or poverty of spirit towards others, fostering humility
key_terms.حُسْنِ الْبِشْرِ: Goodness of countenance or pleasant appearance

ai.seo_question: How to balance humility and self-sufficiency in social interactions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith articulates the Shia ethical ideal of 'Istighna' (spiritual self-sufficiency) balanced with 'Iftiqar' (relational humility), ensuring that social grace stems from choice rather than need. This dual state prevents the degradation of dignity during interaction while preserving inner independence, a concept deeply rooted in the sermons of Imam Ali as a model for moral conduct in community life.
